Regarding wheat and barley, however, no one in Baghdad looked at them at all.
In Mosul, however, along with sickness and pestilence,
famine also occurred because of locusts;
and a kor of wheat was sold for sixty dinars.
And in the year 442,
442 of the Arabs,
which is the year 1361,
1361 of the Greeks,
Sultan Tughril Beg sent an envoy to Ibn Marwan, ruler of Armenia,
that he should submit to his obedience.
And he, Ibn Marwan, received the envoy with joy,
and gave him thirty prime garments,
and five hundred dinars,
and hangings,
and ten mules laden with goods,
and an Arab horse,
and a certain prisoner from the Byzantine nobles, for whom the Byzantines had offered thirty thousand dinars as his ransom, but he had not sold him.
And he said:
"Apart from this, I have no gift that is worthy of Sultan Tughril Beg."
And when he, Tughril Beg, received these things,
he made a fine peace with Ibn Marwan.
Then Constantine, king of the Byzantines, sent to Ibn Marwan:
"I desire that you strive for the release of that patrician;
and I know that Sultan Tughril Beg is magnanimous,
and he will not withhold him if you ask him from him on my behalf."
And when Ibn Marwan made known the words of the king of the Byzantines to Tughril Beg,
he displayed magnanimity,
and sent him with his envoy to the king,
without demanding a ransom or an exchange.
Then the king of the Byzantines renovated {OCR?} the great mosque of the Arabs in the royal city,
and hung lamps in it,
and appointed Arab prayer-leaders in it,
and assigned them allowances.
And he sent to Tughril Beg a thousand pieces of satin,
and five hundred other various garments,
and five hundred horses,
and three hundred Egyptian asses,
and a thousand white goats whose eyes and horns were black,
and were close to donkeys in their size.
And in this year,
when the people of the city of Isfahan were hard-pressed by the siege with which Tughril Beg besieged them—
for he sat against them for nine months—
they sent to the Caliph to intercede with Tughril Beg on their behalf.
